assignedReviews.card_evidence: Walter G. Rosen coined the term in 1985 as a short form of "biological diversity"!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the importance of the six-kingdom system and the three-domain system of classification of living things
assignedReviews.reason: The card only explains who coined the term 'biodiversity' and when. It provides no information about the six-kingdom system or the three-domain system of classification, which is the subject of G8-L-6. The content is unrelated to taxonomic classification.

copy.en:
Who first used the word "biodiversity"?

Walter G. Rosen coined the term in 1985 as a short form of "biological diversity"!
copy.tl:
Sino ang unang gumamit ng salitang "biodiversity"?

Si Walter G. Rosen ang nag-imbento ng termino noong 1985 bilang maikling anyo ng "biological diversity"!
copy.bis:
Kinsa ang unang migamit sa pulong nga "biodiversity"?

Si Walter G. Rosen ang nag-imbento sa termino sa 1985 isip mubo nga porma sa "biological diversity"!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Orion appears to move upward from evening to midnight, then downward from midnight toward dawn.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make suggestions about the importance of the Sun to living things for a group or class discussion and confirm and record ideas by referring to trustworthy secondary sources
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the apparent nightly motion of the constellation Orion. G4-E-9 is about the importance of the Sun to living things and making suggestions for a class discussion. There is no connection to the Sun's importance or to living things; the card is unrelated to the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Orion appears to move upward from evening to midnight, then downward from midnight toward dawn.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe sources of light and their use in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: G3-F-5 requires describing sources of light and their use in everyday situations. The card is about the apparent movement of a constellation at night, not about any light source or its uses. It does not support the competency.

copy.en: Orion appears to move upward from evening to midnight, then downward from midnight toward dawn.
copy.tl: Ang Orion ay parang umaakyat mula gabi hanggang hatinggabi, pagkatapos bumababa mula hatinggabi hanggang madaling araw.
copy.bis: Ang Orion morag mosaka gikan sa gabii hangtod sa tungang gabii, dayon monaog gikan sa tungang gabii hangtod sa kaadlawon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Drinking too fast can make you vomit
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and labeled diagrams the parts of the digestive system as mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, and large intestine, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives advice on how to drink ORS to avoid vomiting. It does not identify or describe any parts of the digestive system (mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, large intestine) or explain how they work. The mention of vomiting is not instruction on digestive system anatomy or function.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Drinking too fast can make you vomit
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe any human body system (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) or how they work. It is a health tip about ORS intake, unrelated to the competency's content.

copy.en:
How should you drink ORS?

Slowly, in small sips every few minutes — not gulped all at once! Drinking too fast can make you vomit.
copy.tl:
Paano dapat inumin ang ORS?

Dahan-dahan, kaunti-kaunting hithit tuwing ilang minuto — huwag inuubos agad! Kapag binigla, mas madaling masuka.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pag-inom sa ORS?

Hinay-hinay, gamay-gamay nga higop kada pipila ka minuto — ayaw ubsa dayon! Kon kalit, sayon masuka.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Yes! For children's diarrhea, doctors recommend giving ORS together with zinc for several days.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses ORS and zinc treatment for childhood diarrhea, which is a medical/health topic. It does not address the basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter) as required by G3-L-6. The content is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en:
Is ORS given with any other medicine?

Yes! For children's diarrhea, doctors recommend giving ORS together with zinc for several days. ORS handles the fluids, while zinc speeds up recovery and reduces future diarrhea.
copy.tl:
May kasama bang gamot ang ORS?

Oo! Sa pagtatae ng bata, inirerekomenda ng doktor ang ORS at zinc ng ilang araw. ORS humahawak ng tubig, zinc pampabilis ng paggaling, pampabawas ng susunod na pagtatae.
copy.bis:
Aduna bay kauban nga tambal ang ORS?

Oo! Sa kalibang sa bata, girekomenda sa doktor ang ORS ug zinc sa pipila ka adlaw. ORS mag-atiman sa tubig, zinc pampaspas sa pagkaayo, pampabawas sa sunod nga kalibang.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An ostrich protects itself from enemies by running fast
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: relate the shape of a volcano's cone to its composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about ostrich behavior and locomotion, completely unrelated to volcano cone shape and composition.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An ostrich protects itself from enemies by running fast
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different types of volcanoes found around the world according to their: a. activity b. type of eruption c. location in the crust
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes ostrich defense mechanisms, not volcano types, eruption styles, or crustal location.

copy.en: An ostrich protects itself from enemies by running fast, using its long strong legs to escape danger.
copy.tl: Pinoprotektahan ng ostrich ang sarili sa mga kaaway sa pamamagitan ng mabilis na pagtakbo, gamit ang mahahabang malalakas na binti.
copy.bis: Ang ostrich moprotektar sa iyang kaugalingon batok sa mga kaaway pinaagi sa kusog nga pagdagan, gamit ang tag-as ug lig-on nga mga tiil.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Outer rainbands bring occasional light to moderate rainfall with winds up to 62 kilometers per hour far from the center.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the root and shoot system in plants and describe why they are important
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes outer rainbands of a tropical cyclone (weather phenomenon), which has no connection to the root and shoot system of plants. The competency G4-L-2 is about plant anatomy and function, so the assigned code is unrelated to the card content.

copy.en: Outer rainbands bring occasional light to moderate rainfall with winds up to 62 kilometers per hour far from the center.
copy.tl: Ang outer rainbands ay nagdadala ng paminsan-minsang mahina hanggang katamtamang ulan na may hangin hanggang 62 kilometers per hour malayo sa gitna.
copy.bis: Ang outer rainbands nagdala ug panagsa nga hinay hangtod kasarangan nga ulan nga adunay hangin hangtod 62 kilometers per hour layo sa tunga.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Oviparous animals are animals that lay eggs
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes oviparous animals (egg-laying animals), which is a biology topic about animal reproduction. G6-M-4 requires describing useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures such as solutions and suspensions. There is no connection to mixtures, solutions, or suspensions.

copy.en: Oviparous animals are animals that lay eggs, and their babies develop outside the mother's body.
copy.tl: Ang mga oviparous na hayop ay nangingitlog, at ang kanilang mga anak ay lumalaki sa labas ng katawan ng ina.
copy.bis: Ang mga oviparous nga mananap mao ang mga mananap nga mangitlog, ug ang ilang mga anak motubo sa gawas sa lawas sa inahan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: each ovule holds a female sex cell that can become a seed after fertilization
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: predict simple ratios of offspring genotypes and phenotypes in crosses involving dominant/recessive gene pairs
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes ovules and fertilization in flowers, which is plant reproduction. It does not address genotypes, phenotypes, dominant/recessive gene pairs, or predicting ratios in crosses, which are the core of G8-L-5.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: each ovule holds a female sex cell that can become a seed after fertilization
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: represent patterns of inheritance of a simple dominant/ recessive characteristic through generations of a family
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses ovules and seed formation, not the representation of inheritance patterns of a dominant/recessive characteristic through generations of a family. No pedigree or trait transmission is mentioned.

copy.en: Inside the ovary of a flower are small round ovules, and each ovule holds a female sex cell that can become a seed after fertilization.
copy.tl: Sa loob ng ovary ng bulaklak ay may maliliit na bilog na ovule, at bawat ovule ay may hawak na female sex cell na maaaring maging buto pagkatapos ng fertilization.
copy.bis: Sa sulod sa ovary sa bulaklak adunay gagmay nga lingin nga mga ovule, ug ang matag ovule nagkupot ug female sex cell nga mahimong liso human sa fertilization.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: P waves are the fastest kind of seismic waves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and record changes in the weather during a day or over some days and describe the different types and patterns of weather in the local area
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the speed of P waves (seismic waves) and why they arrive first at a seismic station. G3-E-4 is about observing and recording weather changes and describing local weather patterns. Seismic waves are unrelated to weather, so the tag is incorrect.

copy.en:
Why are P waves the first to arrive at a seismic station?

P waves are the fastest kind of seismic waves, traveling at about 4 to 6 kilometers per second, so they reach the seismograph before any other wave!
copy.tl:
Bakit P waves ang unang dumadating sa seismic station?

Ang P waves ang pinakamabilis na uri ng seismic waves, na naglalakbay ng mga 4 hanggang 6 na kilometro bawat segundo, kaya nauuna silang makarating sa seismograph kaysa sa ibang alon!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga ang P waves mao man ang unang moabot sa seismic station?

Ang P waves mao ang pinakapaspas nga klase sa seismic waves, nga mobiyahe ug mga 4 hangtod 6 ka kilometro kada segundo, mao nga una silang makaabot sa seismograph kaysa sa uban nga balod!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: As a pendulum swings down, potential energy is lost and kinetic energy is gained, so the total mechanical energy stays the same.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes energy transformation in a pendulum (potential to kinetic, conservation of mechanical energy), which is a physics topic. G6-M-4 requires describing useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions. The card provides no information about mixtures, so it does not support this competency.

copy.en: As a pendulum swings down, potential energy is lost and kinetic energy is gained, so the total mechanical energy stays the same.
copy.tl: Habang bumababa ang pendulum, nababawasan ang potential energy at nadadagdagan ang kinetic energy, kaya ang total mechanical energy ay nananatiling pareho.
copy.bis: Samtang ang pendulum nag-swing paubos, ang potential energy mawala ug ang kinetic energy madugangan, busa ang total mechanical energy nagpabilin nga pareho.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The pancreas makes digestive enzymes, which are helpers that break down food, and bicarbonate, which lowers the acid from the stomach.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the changes of state in terms of particle arrangement and energy changes: a. solid → liquid → vapor, and b. vapor → liquid → solid
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the pancreas's digestive functions (enzymes and bicarbonate). It contains no information about changes of state, particle arrangement, or energy changes, which are the focus of G7-M-5.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of heat energy in change of state processes
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about pancreatic digestive secretions, not about the role of heat energy in change of state processes. No connection to melting, evaporation, freezing, or condensation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The pancreas makes digestive enzymes, which are helpers that break down food, and bicarbonate, which lowers the acid from the stomach.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses digestion and acid neutralization, not how temperature changes cause matter to change state. It does not support the competency's content.

copy.en: The pancreas makes digestive enzymes, which are helpers that break down food, and bicarbonate, which lowers the acid from the stomach.
copy.tl: Ang pancreas ay gumagawa ng digestive enzymes, mga katulong na tumutunaw ng pagkain, at bicarbonate, na nagpapababa ng acid mula sa tiyan.
copy.bis: Ang pancreas mohimo ug digestive enzymes, mga katabang nga motunaw sa pagkaon, ug bicarbonate, nga magpaubos sa acid gikan sa tiyan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The word pangolin comes from the Malay word 'pengguling,' meaning 'one that rolls up'
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card only explains the etymology of the word 'pangolin' and the behavior of curling into a ball. It does not describe any example of an animal changing to better suit its environment, such as mimicry or camouflage, which is the focus of G5-L-9.

copy.en:
Where does 'pangolin' come from?

The word pangolin comes from the Malay word 'pengguling,' meaning 'one that rolls up' — because it curls into a tight ball!
copy.tl:
Saan galing ang salitang pangolin?

Ang salitang pangolin ay mula sa Malay na 'pengguling,' na ang ibig sabihin ay 'isang gumugulong' — dahil tumitiklop ito na parang bola!
copy.bis:
Diin gikan ang pulong pangolin?

Ang pulong pangolin gikan sa Malay nga 'pengguling,' nga nagpasabot og 'usa nga molingin' — kay molingin man kini nga sama sa bola!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Cutting or tearing paper into triangles creates the shapes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the structures, movements and events that occur at each type of plate boundary
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about cutting paper to make banderitas (triangular flags) and notes that paper remains paper after cutting. It has no content about plate boundaries, their structures, movements, or events. The assigned competency is entirely unrelated.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Cutting or tearing paper into triangles creates the shapes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the types of plate boundaries found around the Earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a simple paper-cutting activity, not the types of plate boundaries found around the Earth. There is no instructional support for this earth science competency.

copy.en:
How can cutting paper make banderitas?

Cutting or tearing paper into triangles creates the shapes, and the paper is still paper even after it is cut.
copy.tl:
Paano nakakagawa ng banderitas ang paggupit ng papel?

Ang paggupit o pagpunit ng papel na hugis tatsulok ang lumilikha ng mga hugis, at ang papel ay papel pa rin kahit naputol na.
copy.bis:
Giunsa paghimo sa pagputol sa papel ang mga banderitas?

Ang pagputol o paggisi sa papel nga porma trianggulo maoy naghimo sa mga porma, ug ang papel papel lang gihapon bisan naputol na.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Using many appliances at the same time in a parallel circuit can overload it
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about electrical circuits and overloading, which is physics/technology content. G4-L-1 requires describing human body systems (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory). There is no connection to living things or body systems.

copy.en: Using many appliances at the same time in a parallel circuit can overload it, because each extra appliance draws more current through the wires.
copy.tl: Ang sabay-sabay na paggamit ng maraming appliances sa parallel circuit ay maaaring magdulot ng overloading, dahil bawat dagdag na appliance ay humihila ng mas maraming current sa mga wire.
copy.bis: Ang dungan nga paggamit ug daghang appliances sa parallel circuit makapahinabo ug overloading, tungod kay ang matag dugang nga appliance mobira ug mas daghang current sa mga wire.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Lines of latitude are called parallels because they run east to west and stay parallel to the equator and to each other, never meeting.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the changes of state in terms of particle arrangement and energy changes: a. solid → liquid → vapor, and b. vapor → liquid → solid
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes lines of latitude (parallels), a geography/earth science concept. G7-M-5 requires explaining changes of state in terms of particle arrangement and energy changes. There is no connection to matter, particles, or state changes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Lines of latitude are called parallels because they run east to west and stay parallel to the equator and to each other, never meeting.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of heat energy in change of state processes
assignedReviews.reason: G6-M-2 requires explaining the role of heat energy in change of state processes. The card is about latitude lines and contains no information about heat energy or state changes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Lines of latitude are called parallels because they run east to west and stay parallel to the equator and to each other, never meeting.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: G6-M-1 requires describing changes of state (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation) using diagrams and flowcharts. The card is about parallels of latitude and does not address any state change process.

copy.en: Lines of latitude are called parallels because they run east to west and stay parallel to the equator and to each other, never meeting.
copy.tl: Ang mga linya ng latitude ay tinatawag na parallels dahil tumatakbo ang mga ito mula silangan pakanluran at nananatiling parallel sa equator at sa isa't isa, kaya hindi sila nagtatagpo.
copy.bis: Ang mga linya sa latitude gitawag og parallels tungod kay kini modagan sa silangan paingon sa kasadpan ug magpabiling parallel sa equator ug sa usag usa, busa dili kini magtagbo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Parasitism is a relationship where one organism benefits and the other is harmed
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to name and describe the upper crustal layers of the solid earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a biological relationship (parasitism) and has no content about the upper crustal layers of the solid earth. The assigned competency is entirely unrelated to the card's subject.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Parasitism is a relationship where one organism benefits and the other is harmed
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that the non-living materials that make up the environment are referred to as 'earth materials'
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about a living-things interaction, not about non-living earth materials. It does not support recognizing that non-living materials are called 'earth materials'.

copy.en: Parasitism is a relationship where one organism benefits and the other is harmed but not always killed, so the parasite benefits while the host suffers.
copy.tl: Ang parasitism ay isang relasyon kung saan ang isang organismo ay nakikinabang at ang isa ay nasasaktan ngunit hindi laging namamatay, kaya ang parasite ay nakikinabang habang ang host ay nagdurusa.
copy.bis: Ang parasitism usa ka relasyon diin ang usa ka organismo makabenepisyo ug ang usa masakitan apan dili kanunay mamatay, busa ang parasite makabenepisyo samtang ang host mag-antos.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A duplicated chromosome has two sister chromatids
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes chromosome structure (sister chromatids, centromere, arms, telomeres), which is genetics/biology content. G6-M-1 requires describing changes of state of solids, liquids, and gases (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation) using diagrams and flowcharts. No overlap in subject matter.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A duplicated chromosome has two sister chromatids
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about chromosome parts, not about how temperature changes cause matter to change state (solid to liquid to gas). The assigned competency is entirely unrelated to the card content.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A duplicated chromosome has two sister chromatids
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the changes of state in terms of particle arrangement and energy changes: a. solid → liquid → vapor, and b. vapor → liquid → solid
assignedReviews.reason: G7-M-5 requires explaining changes of state in terms of particle arrangement and energy changes. The card discusses chromosome anatomy, not particle models or phase changes. No instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: A duplicated chromosome has two sister chromatids joined at a narrow centromere, with a shorter p arm, a longer q arm, and protective telomeres at the ends.
copy.tl: Ang duplicated chromosome ay may dalawang sister chromatids na pinagdugtong sa makitid na centromere, may mas maikling p arm, mas mahabang q arm, at protective telomeres sa dulo.
copy.bis: Ang duplicated chromosome adunay duha ka sister chromatids nga gitaod sa hiktin nga centromere, adunay mas mubo nga p arm, mas taas nga q arm, ug protective telomeres sa tumoy.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The main parts of a lever are the effort, the fulcrum, the resistance, the effort arm, and the resistance arm.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the chemical properties of materials, such as they can be burnt, react with other materials, or are degradable or biodegradable
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the parts of a lever, a simple machine. It contains no information about chemical properties of materials such as burning, reactivity, or biodegradability, which is the subject of G4-M-3.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The main parts of a lever are the effort, the fulcrum, the resistance, the effort arm, and the resistance arm.

assignedReviews.reason: The card is about lever anatomy, not about minimizing harmful changes in materials (e.g., restricting burning of waste or handling reactive materials). It does not support G4-M-5 in any way.

copy.en: The main parts of a lever are the effort, the fulcrum, the resistance, the effort arm, and the resistance arm.
copy.tl: Ang mga pangunahing parte ng lever ay ang effort, fulcrum, resistance, effort arm, at resistance arm.
copy.bis: Ang mga pangunang parte sa lever mao ang effort, fulcrum, resistance, effort arm, ug resistance arm.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A simple circuit is composed of a voltage source
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of pure substances as: a. having fixed chemical composition, examples of which are elements and compounds, and b. that all the atoms of an element have a unique number of protons
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the components of a simple electrical circuit (voltage source, wires, switch, load). It does not address pure substances, fixed chemical composition, elements/compounds, or protons, which are the focus of G8-M-4.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A simple circuit is composed of a voltage source
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the names and symbols of the first 20 or several common elements of the periodic table
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about circuit components, not the names and symbols of elements in the periodic table. It provides no support for identifying elements or their symbols.

copy.en: A simple circuit is composed of a voltage source like a battery, connecting wires, a switch, and a load such as a bulb or resistor.
copy.tl: Ang simpleng circuit ay binubuo ng voltage source tulad ng battery, connecting wires, switch, at load gaya ng bulb o resistor.
copy.bis: Ang simple nga circuit gilangkuban sa voltage source sama sa battery, connecting wires, switch, ug load sama sa bulb o resistor.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Why do we present possible solutions to the class before doing them?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how plant organs (leaf, stem, roots) work together as the transport system
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses peer evaluation of proposed solutions in a science activity. It has no content about plant organs (leaf, stem, roots) or the transport system, so it does not support the competency in any way.

copy.en:
Why do we present possible solutions to the class before doing them?

So classmates can evaluate them, which means they share ideas and suggestions that can make the solution even better.
copy.tl:
Bakit natin ipinapakita ang mga posibleng solusyon sa klase bago gawin?

Para ma-evaluate ito ng mga kaklase, na nangangahulugang nagbabahagi sila ng mga ideya at mungkahi na makakapagpabuti pa sa solusyon.
copy.bis:
Ngano atong ipakita ang posible nga solusyon sa klase sa dili pa buhaton?

Aron ma-evaluate kini sa mga klasmeyt, nga nagpasabot nga sila mopaambit og mga ideya ug sugyot nga makapauswag pa sa solusyon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: People break down rocks through activities like mining, quarrying, building roads, and farming, which physically break rocks into smaller pieces.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes human activities that physically break rocks into smaller pieces (physical weathering). G5-E-11 requires describing the general structure of the solar system, major celestial objects, and their features/composition. The card has no connection to the solar system.

copy.en: People break down rocks through activities like mining, quarrying, building roads, and farming, which physically break rocks into smaller pieces.
copy.tl: Binabasag ng mga tao ang mga bato sa pamamagitan ng mga gawain tulad ng pagmimina, pag-quarry, paggawa ng kalsada, at pagsasaka, na pisikal na naghahati sa mga bato sa maliliit na piraso.
copy.bis: Ang mga tawo magpikas sa mga bato pinaagi sa mga kalihokan sama sa pagmina, pag-quarry, paghimo og karsada, ug pag-uma, nga pisikal nga nagbahin sa mga bato ngadto sa gagmayng mga piraso.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Divide the change in momentum by the starting momentum, then multiply by 100 to get the percentage of momentum lost.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: construct and annotate distance-time graphs and velocity-time graphs to represent uniform and non-uniform acceleration
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains how to calculate percentage of momentum lost. It does not involve constructing or annotating distance-time or velocity-time graphs, nor does it address uniform or non-uniform acceleration. The topic is momentum, not graph construction.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Divide the change in momentum by the starting momentum, then multiply by 100 to get the percentage of momentum lost.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: construct and label simple graphs of different speeds including stationary and uniform speeds, both fast and slow
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about momentum loss calculation, not about constructing or labeling simple graphs of speeds. It does not support the competency of graphing stationary or uniform speeds.

copy.en:
How can you tell how much momentum a ball lost?

Divide the change in momentum by the starting momentum, then multiply by 100 to get the percentage of momentum lost.
copy.tl:
Paano malalaman kung gaano karaming momentum ang nawala sa bola?

I-divide ang change in momentum sa starting momentum, tapos i-multiply sa 100 para makuha ang percentage ng momentum lost.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagkahibalo kung pila ka momentum ang nawala sa bola?

Bahina ang change in momentum sa starting momentum, dayon i-multiply sa 100 aron makuha ang percentage sa momentum lost.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Periods are considered fundamental time intervals because they are the divisions most often associated with distinct fossil clues.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses geological periods and fossils, which is unrelated to sound production or transfer. It does not support the competency about exploring and describing how sound is made and transferred.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Periods are considered fundamental time intervals because they are the divisions most often associated with distinct fossil clues.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: research using secondary sources to identify how the properties of waves are described using scientific terms such as amplitude, frequency, wavelength, and velocity
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about geological time periods and fossils, not about wave properties such as amplitude, frequency, wavelength, or velocity. It provides no instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: Periods are considered fundamental time intervals because they are the divisions most often associated with distinct fossil clues.
copy.tl: Itinuturing na pangunahing mga pagitan ng panahon ang mga period dahil ito ang mga dibisyon na kadalasang nauugnay sa natatanging mga pahiwatig mula sa fossil.
copy.bis: Ang mga period giisip nga sukaranan nga mga gidugayon sa panahon tungod kay kini ang mga dibisyon nga kasagarang nalangkit sa lahi nga mga timailhan sa fossil.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: If a story is sacred or private, don't put it on a poster!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from local indigenous community members or from reliable secondary sources to investigate ways that indigenous people of the Philippines represented and communicated understandings of the predictability of solar and lunar eclipses, and patterns/interpretations in the night sky and their use for tracking time
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses respecting private/sacred stories and asking permission before sharing in class. It has no connection to indigenous Philippine knowledge of eclipses, night sky patterns, or time tracking, which is the subject of G6-E-10.

copy.en:
Can you share any story in class?

If a story is sacred or private, don't put it on a poster! Ask what can be shared with the class, and respect a "no."
copy.tl:
Pwede bang ibahagi ang anumang kwento sa klase?

Kung ang kwento ay sagrado o pribado, huwag mong ilagay sa poster! Tanungin kung ano ang pwedeng ibahagi, at igalang ang "hindi."
copy.bis:
Pwede ba nga ipaambit ang bisan unsang istorya sa klase?

Kung ang istorya sagrado o pribado, ayaw ibutang sa poster! Pangutan-a kung unsa ang pwede i-share, ug respetuhi ang "dili."

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the oceanic Nazca Plate subducts beneath the continental South American Plate
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some examples of longitudinal waves, and transverse waves
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes plate subduction at the Peru-Chile Trench, a geology/plate-tectonics topic. It provides no information about longitudinal or transverse waves, which is the subject of G6-F-9.

copy.en: Off the coast of South America, the oceanic Nazca Plate subducts beneath the continental South American Plate along the Peru-Chile Trench.
copy.tl: Sa baybayin ng South America, ang oceanic Nazca Plate ay sumusubduct sa ilalim ng continental South American Plate sa Peru-Chile Trench.
copy.bis: Sa baybayon sa South America, ang oceanic Nazca Plate mosubduct ilalom sa continental South American Plate ubay sa Peru-Chile Trench.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Some mixtures are described by phase pairings
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain properties of metals in terms of their structure and metallic bonding (sea of electrons model)
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses phase pairings of mixtures (solid in liquid, liquid in liquid). G9-M-10 requires explaining properties of metals in terms of metallic bonding and the sea of electrons model. The card has no connection to metals, metallic structure, or bonding.

copy.en: Some mixtures are described by phase pairings like solid in liquid, such as powdered milk in water, or liquid in liquid, such as alcohol in water.
copy.tl: Ang ilang mixtures ay inilalarawan sa pamamagitan ng phase pairings tulad ng solid in liquid, gaya ng powdered milk sa tubig, o liquid in liquid, gaya ng alcohol sa tubig.
copy.bis: Ang uban nga mga mixtures gihulagway pinaagi sa phase pairings sama sa solid in liquid, sama sa powdered milk sa tubig, o liquid in liquid, sama sa alcohol sa tubig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It has a wingspan of about 7 feet
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how solar energy contributes to the occurrence of land and sea breezes, monsoons, and the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the Philippine eagle's wingspan, eyesight, and talons. It contains no information about solar energy, land/sea breezes, monsoons, or the ITCZ, so it does not support this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: eyes that see eight times clearer than human eyes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about eagle size and senses, not about weather characteristics such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, or cloud cover. It is unrelated to this competency.

copy.en:
How powerful is the Philippine eagle?

It has a wingspan of about 7 feet, eyes that see eight times clearer than human eyes, and strong talons that can cut through prey easily!
copy.tl:
Gaano kalakas ang Philippine eagle?

Mayroon itong wingspan na humigit-kumulang 7 talampakan, mga matang nakakakita nang walong beses na mas malinaw kaysa mata ng tao, at malalakas na talon na kayang humiwa sa biktima nang madali!
copy.bis:
Unsa ka kusgan ang Philippine eagle?

Kini adunay wingspan nga mga 7 ka tiil, mga mata nga makakita ug walo ka pilo nga mas tin-aw kay sa mata sa tawo, ug kusgan nga mga talon nga makahimo sa paghiwa sa biktima nga dali!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Does food in a plant only move downward from the leaves?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how energy from the Sun interacts with the atmosphere
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses phloem transport of sugars in plants, which is plant physiology. G7-E-9 requires explaining how solar energy interacts with the atmosphere, an Earth/space topic. No instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Does food in a plant only move downward from the leaves?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe some of the overall characteristics of the Sun, such as its composition, its size, and the main energy it radiates
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about phloem food movement in plants, not about the Sun's composition, size, or radiated energy. G4-E-7 is an Earth/space competency about the Sun; the card is unrelated.

copy.en:
Does food in a plant only move downward from the leaves?

Mostly yes, but phloem can also move sugars to growing buds and roots that need energy, so food flows to wherever the plant needs it!
copy.tl:
Pababa lang ba mula sa dahon ang pagkain sa halaman?

Kadalasan oo, ngunit kaya ring ilipat ng phloem ang sugars sa mga tumutubong bud at ugat na nangangailangan ng enerhiya, kaya dumadaloy ang pagkain kung saan ito kailangan ng halaman!
copy.bis:
Paubos lang ba ang pagkaon sa tanom gikan sa dahon?

Kasagaran oo, apan ang phloem makabalhin usab sa sugars ngadto sa nagtubo nga mga bud ug gamot nga nagkinahanglan ug enerhiya, busa moagos ang pagkaon bisan asa kini gikinahanglan sa tanom!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Phosphodiester bonds connect nucleotides together
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the relative wavelengths and frequencies of different types of electromagnetic waves, including radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultra-violet, x-rays, and gamma radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the chemical structure of DNA (phosphodiester bonds), which is unrelated to comparing wavelengths and frequencies of electromagnetic waves.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Phosphodiester bonds connect nucleotides together
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe electromagnetic radiation (EMR) as energy that is created by the vibrations of electrically charged particles which allows it to travel through materials or space as transverse waves
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about DNA backbone chemistry, not electromagnetic radiation or transverse waves.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Phosphodiester bonds connect nucleotides together
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that waves carry energy from a source to a receiver
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not address waves carrying energy; it is about molecular bonds in DNA.

copy.en: Phosphodiester bonds connect nucleotides together by joining a phosphate group to the pentose sugar, forming the DNA backbone.
copy.tl: Ang phosphodiester bonds ang nagdudugtong sa mga nucleotides sa pamamagitan ng pag-join ng phosphate group sa pentose sugar, na bumubuo sa DNA backbone.
copy.bis: Ang phosphodiester bonds mao ang nagdugtong sa mga nucleotides pinaagi sa pag-join sa phosphate group ngadto sa pentose sugar, nga nagporma sa DNA backbone.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A phreatic eruption is a steam-driven blast that happens when hot rocks touch water, turning it instantly into steam.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a phreatic (volcanic) eruption, which is a volcanic process. G5-E-11 requires describing the general structure of the solar system and major celestial objects. The card provides no information about the solar system, planets, stars, or celestial composition, so it is unrelated to the assigned competency.

copy.en: A phreatic eruption is a steam-driven blast that happens when hot rocks touch water, turning it instantly into steam.
copy.tl: Ang phreatic eruption ay isang steam-driven na pagsabog na nangyayari kapag ang maiinit na bato ay dumikit sa tubig, na agad itong ginagawang singaw.
copy.bis: Ang phreatic eruption usa ka steam-driven nga pagbuto nga mahitabo kung ang init nga mga bato modapat sa tubig, nga dayon kini himoong alisngaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Many respiratory diseases like colds, cough, asthma, and chronic bronchitis are first detected through a physical examination by a doctor.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify examples of everyday situations that demonstrate: a. kinetic energy being transformed to potential energy, and b. potential energy being transformed to kinetic energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses detection of respiratory diseases via physical examination. It contains no information about kinetic energy transforming to potential energy or vice versa, which is the sole subject of G8-F-5.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Many respiratory diseases like colds, cough, asthma, and chronic bronchitis are first detected through a physical examination by a doctor.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe kinetic energy as the movement of objects or particles, and potential energy as energy stored due to the position of objects or particles
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about medical diagnosis of respiratory conditions, not about kinetic energy as movement or potential energy as stored energy. It provides no instructional support for G8-F-4.

copy.en: Many respiratory diseases like colds, cough, asthma, and chronic bronchitis are first detected through a physical examination by a doctor.
copy.tl: Maraming sakit sa paghinga tulad ng sipon, ubo, hika, at chronic bronchitis ang unang natutukoy sa pamamagitan ng physical examination ng doktor.
copy.bis: Daghang sakit sa pagginhawa sama sa sip-on, ubo, hika, ug chronic bronchitis ang unang maila pinaagi sa physical examination sa doktor.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Length, mass, time, volume, and temperature are physical quantities because they can all be measured.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines measurable physical quantities, which is unrelated to describing the general structure of the solar system, celestial objects, their features, or composition.

copy.en: Length, mass, time, volume, and temperature are physical quantities because they can all be measured.
copy.tl: Ang length, mass, time, volume, at temperature ay mga physical quantity dahil lahat sila ay maaaring sukatin.
copy.bis: Ang length, mass, time, volume, ug temperature mga physical quantity kay silang tanan mahimo nga sukdon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Benguet Pine survives freezing mountain weather
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that the arrangement of elements in the periodic table as 7 periods and 18 groups is based on their atomic structure and chemical properties, such as reactivity
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a plant adaptation to cold (needle-like leaves and cone shape), which has no connection to the periodic table, atomic structure, or chemical properties of elements.

copy.en: The Benguet Pine survives freezing mountain weather with needle-like leaves that lose little water and a cone shape that lets snow slide off instead of breaking branches.
copy.tl: Nabubuhay ang Benguet Pine sa nagyeyelong panahon sa bundok dahil sa mala-karayom nitong mga dahon na kakaunti lang ang nawawalang tubig at hugis-kono na nagpapadausdos sa snow sa halip na mabali ang mga sanga.
copy.bis: Ang Benguet Pine mabuhi sa nagyelo nga panahon sa bukid tungod sa dagom-dagom nga mga dahon nga gamay ra ang mawala nga tubig ug porma nga kono nga makapadalin-as sa snow imbes nga mabali ang mga sanga.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The pinna not only catches sound waves but also protects the inner parts of the ear.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify issues and concerns in the local community and how they could be addressed by science, such as the treatment of waste
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the function of the pinna in the ear, which is biology/anatomy content. G4-M-6 is about identifying local community issues and how science addresses them, such as waste treatment. There is no connection to community issues, waste, or science addressing local concerns.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The pinna not only catches sound waves but also protects the inner parts of the ear.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate proper handling and disposal of materials according to their properties, such as reusing objects, disposing of excess oil into garbage, and recycling paper, plastic or glass
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about ear anatomy and sound wave capture, not about proper handling and disposal of materials, reusing, recycling, or disposing of waste. G3-M-7 is a matter/materials competency and is unrelated to the card's content.

copy.en: The pinna not only catches sound waves but also protects the inner parts of the ear.
copy.tl: Ang pinna ay hindi lamang sumasagap ng sound waves kundi pinoprotektahan din nito ang mga panloob na bahagi ng tainga.
copy.bis: Ang pinna dili lamang mosagap sa sound waves kondili manalipod usab kini sa mga parte sa sulod sa dalunggan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A plant-based diet produces lower amounts of greenhouse gases than a diet that includes a lot of meat.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe mutations as changes in DNA or chromosomes and discuss some of the factors that cause mutations, such as infectious agents, radiation, and chemicals
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses greenhouse gas emissions from dietary choices, which has no connection to mutations, DNA, or chromosomes. It does not support the competency in any way.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A plant-based diet produces lower amounts of greenhouse gases than a diet that includes a lot of meat.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of DNA, genes, and chromosomes in the transmission of traits
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about diet and greenhouse gases, not about the role of DNA, genes, or chromosomes in trait transmission. It is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: A plant-based diet produces lower amounts of greenhouse gases than a diet that includes a lot of meat.
copy.tl: Ang plant-based diet ay gumagawa ng mas mababang greenhouse gases kaysa sa diet na maraming karne.
copy.bis: Ang plant-based diet maghimo ug mas ubos nga greenhouse gases kaysa sa diet nga daghan ug karne.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: First-order consumers are animals that feed directly on producers
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss how bodies of water and landforms affect typhoons
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains first-order consumers (herbivores) in a food chain, which is ecology content. G8-E-9 requires discussing how bodies of water and landforms affect typhoons, a meteorology/earth science topic. There is no overlap in subject matter.

copy.en: First-order consumers are animals that feed directly on producers, meaning they eat plants, vegetables, or fruits.
copy.tl: Ang first-order consumers ay mga hayop na direktang kumakain sa producers, ibig sabihin kumakain sila ng halaman, gulay, o prutas.
copy.bis: Ang first-order consumers mao ang mga mananap nga direktang mokaon sa producers, nagpasabot nga mokaon sila ug tanom, utanon, o prutas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Plants have specialized structures like thorns, spines, sharp leaves, and bad smells to protect themselves from predators.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe electromagnetic radiation (EMR) as energy that is created by the vibrations of electrically charged particles which allows it to travel through materials or space as transverse waves
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes plant defense structures, which has no relation to electromagnetic radiation, charged particles, or transverse waves. It does not support any part of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Plants have specialized structures like thorns, spines, sharp leaves, and bad smells to protect themselves from predators.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about plant protection mechanisms, not about how sound is made or transferred. It does not support the competency on sound.

copy.en: Plants have specialized structures like thorns, spines, sharp leaves, and bad smells to protect themselves from predators.
copy.tl: Ang mga halaman ay may specialized structures tulad ng tinik, spines, matutulis na dahon, at mabahong amoy para protektahan ang sarili sa mga predator.
copy.bis: Ang mga tanom adunay specialized structures sama sa tunok, spines, hait nga mga dahon, ug baho nga baho aron protektahan ang kaugalingon sa mga predator.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: We can plant new trees, which is called reforestation
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: examine a local weather chart to make simple interpretations about the local weather and describe and practice safety precautions to use during poor or extreme weather conditions
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about reforestation as a solution to deforestation; it contains no weather chart, local weather interpretation, or safety precautions for poor/extreme weather.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: We can plant new trees, which is called reforestation
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not address any weather characteristics such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, or cloud cover.

copy.en:
How can we solve the problem of deforestation?

We can plant new trees, which is called reforestation, to bring back forests and help the environment.
copy.tl:
Paano natin masosolusyunan ang problema ng deforestation?

Maaari tayong magtanim ng mga bagong puno, na tinatawag na reforestation, upang maibalik ang mga kagubatan at makatulong sa kapaligiran.
copy.bis:
Giunsa nato masulbad ang problema sa deforestation?

Makatanom kita og mga bag-ong kahoy, nga gitawag og reforestation, aron mabalik ang mga kalasangan ug makatabang sa kalikopan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: all plants are composed of cells
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes Schleiden's cell theory for plants, which is a biology topic about cellular composition, not the physical properties of solid materials (hard, shiny, stretchable) as required by G3-M-5.

copy.en: In 1838, German botanist Matthias Schleiden studied many plants and concluded that all plants are composed of cells.
copy.tl: Noong 1838, pinag-aralan ng German botanist na si Matthias Schleiden ang maraming halaman at napagpasyahan na ang lahat ng halaman ay binubuo ng mga cell.
copy.bis: Niadtong 1838, gitun-an sa German botanist nga si Matthias Schleiden ang daghang tanom ug mihinapos nga ang tanang tanom gilangkuban sa mga cell.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Plants release oxygen into the air
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about plants producing oxygen for breathing, which is a life-science concept. G6-M-4 requires describing useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures (solutions and suspensions). The card provides no information about mixtures, solutions, or suspensions, so it does not support this competency at all.

copy.en: Plants release oxygen into the air, and without them, humans and animals would have less fresh air to breathe.
copy.tl: Ang mga halaman ay naglalabas ng oxygen sa hangin, at kung wala sila, ang mga tao at hayop ay magkakaroon ng mas kaunting sariwang hangin na malalanghap.
copy.bis: Ang mga tanom nagpagawas ug oxygen sa hangin, ug kung wala sila, ang mga tao ug mananap adunay mas diyutay nga presko nga hangin nga maginhawa.
